judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's recomputation claims hold. Pattern A = 0,2,4,6,8,10 and B = 0,6,12,18,24,30, so 18/6 = 3 and 3*10 = 30 (p3); the pairs (0,0), (2,6), (4,12), (6,18) and the 8 -> 24 extension (p4); Ana 5+3*7 = 26 (p5); Ben 10+6*7 = 52 and 52/26 = 2 (p6); means 55/5 = 11 and 110/5 = 22 (p7); C = 3,5,7,9 and D = 3,7,11,15 so the true fourth term is 15 against Mia's 18 (p8); P = 0,3,6,9,12 with Q = 0,5,10,15,20 and (5/3)*6 = 10 (p9). The three manual entries (4, 9, 10) really do describe what the sheet prints. The judge stopped there. Problem 8 asks the student to 'explain what Mia's rule got wrong' and carries only an eval entry for 15 -- no manual part -- even though the answer key writes a full paragraph for it and prints '(Open response -- judge by reading.)' on problems 4, 9 and 10 but not on 8. Problem 7(c) ('Compare your two means: is the second one twice the first?') is a third printed answer with no entry of any kind; the key answers 'Yes: 22 is twice 11'. So the sheet's own convention for marking open work is applied inconsistently, which the judge's 'all three manual items' framing hides.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 plants the exact misconception the standard targets -- doubling the step does not double the terms when both patterns share a starting number -- and machine-proves the wrong route lands somewhere else: the declared trap 2*(3+2*3) = 18 against the true 3+4*3 = 15. The key's disproof is the cheapest possible one: 'Term 1 shows the claim failing at once: 3 and 3 are equal, not double.'

Problem 10 asks the student to invent a pair of rules whose corresponding terms stay in a 1:4 ratio, and the manual desc plus the key's 'Look for' list demand what actually matters: five terms of each, the relationship holding at EVERY term rather than the last one, and an explanation naming both the start and the step. It closes the loop on problem 8's error instead of repeating it.

The savings context (problems 5-7) reuses the same two patterns as ordinary arithmetic sequences and then asks whether the term-by-term ratio survives averaging. The key answers that properly -- 'a relationship that holds term by term is inherited by the mean' -- which is real reasoning at the top of the Grade 4-5 band, not an extra computation.

root_causes.description: Nothing forces an explanation sub-part to be typed `manual` when its problem already carries a machine entry, so the sheet applies its own convention inconsistently: problems 4, 9 and 10 are flagged, problem 8 -- the sheet's centrepiece error-analysis item -- is not.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 8: '... give the real fourth term of Pattern D, and explain what Mia's rule got wrong.'
verify.json id 8 holds one entry, eval a+d*(n-1) = 15, plus a trap; no manual entry
answer_key.pdf p3 devotes a five-line paragraph to what Mia's rule missed, but prints '(Open response -- judge by reading.)' only on problems 4, 9 and 10
final_response.md: 'Three items are flagged for manual review' -- the explanation in problem 8 is not among them

root_causes.description: Printed answer slots outnumber verify entries on three problems. The comparison in 7(c) has no entry at all, and problems 1 and 2 ask for a six-term list while only the sixth term is checked.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7(c) 'Compare your two means: is the second one twice the first?'; verify.json id 7 holds two stats entries (means 11 and 22) and nothing for the comparison
Problems 1 and 2 print 'Write the first six terms ... then say what its sixth term is'; verify.json checks only a+d*(n-1) at n=6
answer_key.pdf p1 prints the full lists 0,2,4,6,8,10 and 0,6,12,18,24,30

improvements.title: Flag problem 8's 'explain what Mia's rule got wrong' as manual
improvements.proposed_change: Add a manual-coverage gate to the build chain. A new checker (tests/check_manual_coverage.py, wired into scripts/build.sh beside answer-line-ws) segments the worksheet .tex with tests/_tex_segments.py and, for each problem, scans the printed prose for open-response cues -- 'Explain', 'Why did/does', 'Say why', 'What went wrong', 'describe', 'in one or two sentences', 'Which ... did/was' followed by a rule blank, and the drawing verbs 'Plot', 'Shade', 'Draw', 'label' -- and requires the matching id in verify.json to carry at least one entry of type 'manual'. Exit 1 with the offending sentence quoted when it does not. SKILL.md line 257 already states the rule ('Use manual for ... any explanation/reasoning answer'); nothing enforces it, and per-problem coverage (SKILL.md line 189) is satisfied by any single machine entry on the same id.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_manual_coverage.py gains a fixture from problem 8: a segment ending 'give the real fourth term of Pattern D, and explain what Mia's rule got wrong' with a verify.json id 8 holding only the eval for 15. Assert the checker exits 1 and quotes the 'explain' clause; add a manual entry and assert exit 0. The current chain passes this input, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The sheet's own convention becomes uniform: every item the answer key marks '(Open response -- judge by reading.)' is also marked in the verification data, and the reported manual count (3) matches the number of items a human must actually read (4).
improvements.risk: Cue-based flagging can over-trigger on error-analysis items whose 'explain' clause is really answered by the declared trap. Mitigate by reporting manual items as exit 2 rather than a build failure, so a reviewed sheet still ships.

improvements.title: Check the 7(c) comparison and the printed term lists
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the sheet-side gate so coverage is counted per printed response slot, not per problem id. tests/check_answer_line.py already segments the worksheet and reads verify.json; have it also count the response slots each segment prints (\ansblank, \answerline, \ansline, and \underline{\hspace{...}}) and fail when a problem prints more slots than its id has verify entries, unless the surplus is explicitly absorbed by a 'manual' entry. SKILL.md's JSON-format section should state the rule as 'one check per printed blank', replacing today's 'at least one check per problem id'.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_unit_binding.py gains a fixture from problem 7: a segment printing parts (a), (b) and (c) with a verify.json id 7 holding two stats entries. Assert check_answer_line.py exits 1 naming the third slot; add a compare entry (values [22, 11] relation, expected '=' on 22 vs 2*11) and assert exit 0. No slot count exists today, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The mean-doubling conclusion -- the intellectual point of problems 5-7 -- gains a machine check instead of resting on the key's prose, and the six-term lists in problems 1 and 2 stop being unproved.
improvements.risk: Forcing an entry for every list element would bloat the JSON; allow a single sequence-style entry to satisfy a list slot rather than demanding six separate evals.

case_summary: Ten problems on generating and comparing two patterns, every term, ratio, ordered pair, mean and graph coordinate recomputed here and correct. The set is well built: problem 8 plants the double-the-step misconception with a machine-proved trap value, and problem 10 makes the student construct a correct pair of rules, with a manual rubric that insists the relationship hold at every term. The ACCEPT is right. The defect is labelling consistency, not content: problems 4, 9 and 10 are typed `manual` and printed as open responses in the key, while problem 8 -- which explicitly says 'explain what Mia's rule got wrong' -- is recorded as fully machine-checked, and 7(c)'s comparison has no entry at all. final_response.md names all three PDFs, so artifact surfacing is fine here.
